scope: Older or quiet benchmarks beyond standard coding and math leaderboards, with a local-model pilot that is plausibly runnable within five hours.

method.sources: Primary GitHub repositories and the papers linked from them; GitHub REST metadata/history checked for repository activity where available.
method.public_web_lookup: Public GitHub pages and linked papers were checked through web search/open; no interactive browser session or sign-in was used.
method.caution: Historical scores identify tasks worth rechecking; they do not establish modern model unsaturation. No 2026 model run was performed.

recommendations.name: PlanBench
recommendations.pilot: Sample 100 to 200 randomized Mystery Blocksworld or hard PDDL instances; retain plan-validity and goal-completion metrics by split.
recommendations.reason: Strongest practical planning candidate: clear historical failures on controlled tasks and a symbolic evaluator.

recommendations.name: DiscoveryWorld
recommendations.pilot: Use one fixed seed on four to eight easy or challenge scenarios; report completion, procedural progress, and knowledge separately.
recommendations.reason: Uncommon end-to-end scientific discovery tasks with local simulation and built-in scorecards.

recommendations.name: MuSR
recommendations.pilot: Evaluate 100 to 200 items balanced across murder mysteries, object placement, and team allocation using the Hugging Face backend.
recommendations.reason: Narrative reasoning has three distinct inference modes, a fixed test set, and exact multiple-choice scoring.

recommendations.name: StepGame
recommendations.pilot: Score 200 to 500 corrected, noisy examples, stratified by hop count; include k=6 to 10 for generalization.
recommendations.reason: Cheap spatial-reasoning slice with generated labels and a clear correction history.

candidates.name: PlanBench

repository_activity.last_substantive_commit: 2025-05-05, merged upstream planning/results changes; content additions include 2025-04-07
repository_activity.distinction: Leaderboard table is a separate README edit from the later repository merge.

published_top_scores.result: 99.1% Blocksworld NL; 43.3% Mystery Blocksworld NL; 25.8% randomized Mystery Blocksworld NL; 53.6% Blocksworld Hard PDDL
published_top_scores.metric: Plan success / accuracy on the static test sets

license.data: Problem sets and result artifacts are in the repository; no separate dataset license statement found.

candidates.data_access: Public static test sets and model result files in the repository. Local scoring is possible.

evaluator.metric: Whether the proposed plan reaches the goal; PDDL plans can be validated with the supplied planner tooling.
evaluator.deterministic: Yes for a fixed problem and fixed planner/version; generation randomness comes from the model.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A 100 to 200 item pilot should fit; full run time depends on local model speed and planner setup.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: Use a local Hugging Face model or local OpenAI-compatible endpoint; do not use the paid API path.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.caveat: Output format and prompting differ between natural-language and PDDL conditions.

candidates.modern_unsaturation: Unknown. README results end in 2025; low historical randomized-task scores are not proof of current headroom.

candidates.name: MuSR

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: No results table or leaderboard in the repository; paper results are from the 2024 ICLR paper.

published_top_scores.result: 86.0% murder mysteries; 72.3% object placements; 86.8% team allocation

license.data: Dataset files are included in the repository; no separate data license was found.

candidates.data_access: Public JSON test sets in datasets/. The paper describes 750 total examples across three domains.

evaluator.deterministic: Yes after answer-letter parsing; model sampling can change predictions.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A balanced 100 to 200 item local-model pilot is plausible within five hours. Full 750-item timing depends on model throughput and output length.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: The README documents Hugging Face model support. The default example uses OpenAI, which is not required.

candidates.modern_unsaturation: Unknown. No current frontier comparison in the repository or linked paper.

candidates.name: StepGame

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: No official current leaderboard. A separate corrected-dataset LLM evaluation appeared in 2024.

published_top_scores.result: 52.99% mean accuracy over noisy k=1 to 5 test splits; 31.25% at k=5
Cached model responses and corrected-data experiments are provided, but no single comparable SOTA score was found in the repository summary.
published_top_scores.metric: Accuracy by split and prompting condition

license.data: Repository offers generated datasets and a Hugging Face copy; no separate dataset license statement found.

candidates.data_access: Public clean/noisy generated data; use the corrected February 2024 data or the linked Hugging Face dataset.

evaluator.metric: Exact relation-label accuracy by noise and hop count.
evaluator.deterministic: Yes for fixed labels and answer normalization.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A 200 to 500 item slice is plausible within five hours. Avoid running every generated split; the full data collection is large.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: Inference is independent of the generator. Use local models and exact-answer scoring.

candidates.quality_notes: The original repository documents a 2024 template correction. Old scores are neural-network results, not current LLM scores.
candidates.modern_unsaturation: Unknown. No representative current LLM leaderboard found.

candidates.name: SciBench

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: The official site says its GPT results were evaluated 2024-03-15; it currently displays a best overall score of 48.96%.
repository_activity.distinction: The displayed page is current, but the underlying model evaluations are dated 2024-03-15.

published_top_scores.note: The static page exposes the aggregate score but not the model row in its text view; model identity left unknown.

license.data: The repository links a public Hugging Face dataset; confirm the dataset card terms before redistribution.

candidates.data_access: Textbook problems and multimodal files are in the repository; the paper describes 869 total problems, including 177 with visual context. Closed exam data is a separate set.

evaluator.metric: Parsed numeric answer accuracy; the repository also has a separate LLM-based error attribution workflow.
evaluator.deterministic: Numeric matching is deterministic after answer extraction; error attribution is not deterministic and needs an LLM.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A 50 to 100 item text-only pilot is plausible within five hours. Full 869-item evaluation depends on local model throughput and calculator setup.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: Adapt the prompt runner to a local model. The error-analysis script explicitly expects an API key, but it is optional for accuracy scoring.

candidates.quality_notes: Paper-to-repository dataset size/version may differ; pin the downloaded version and report it. This overlaps quantitative reasoning more than the other candidates.
candidates.latest_frontier_score: 48.96% is displayed by the official site, but its accompanying note dates GPT evaluations to 2024-03-15.
candidates.modern_unsaturation: Unknown; the published measurement is old and must not be treated as current headroom.

candidates.name: DiscoveryWorld

repository_activity.latest_non_readme_file_change_found: 2025-01-21, repository cleanup; core data release dates to 2024-06-12
repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: No live leaderboard found; latest benchmark results are from the NeurIPS 2024 paper.

published_top_scores.result: 18% challenge-task completion in the paper's aggregate challenge setting
published_top_scores.metric: Binary task completion; paper separately reports procedural progress and knowledge
published_top_scores.note: Paper table reports scores averaged over seeds; not a current frontier result.

license.data: Paper-run data is linked from the repository. Bundled CuteRPG art assets use separate terms and cannot be resold.

candidates.data_access: Public simulator, scenarios, agent examples, scorecards, and links to full paper run data. The README says installation usually takes minutes and documents Python 3.9.

evaluator.metric: Rule-based task completion, procedural scorecards, and explanatory-knowledge checks.
evaluator.deterministic: Mostly deterministic with a fixed task seed and simulator version; model action selection is stochastic if decoding is.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: Install is documented as minutes. A 4 to 8 task pilot with one seed is plausible within five hours; a full 120-task run is not guaranteed.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: The repository has a small agent API adapter point; connect it to a local model.

candidates.quality_notes: Excellent scientific-discovery task, but simulations are abstractions and do not establish transfer to real scientific research.
candidates.modern_unsaturation: Unknown. Founding-paper baselines are from 2024; no current frontier rerun found.

candidates.name: AbductionRules

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: Static result files and final paper; no later leaderboard found.

published_top_scores.result: 100% exact match on several matched train/test dataset conditions
0% exact match in some unseen domains; paper reports much higher useful-answer rates under relaxed error handling
published_top_scores.metric: Exact string accuracy, with separate relaxed-error analyses

license.data: Dataset files are included with the repository; no distinct data terms found.

candidates.data_access: Public generated train/dev/test sets across animal/person domains and simple/confounded rules.

evaluator.metric: Exact natural-language explanation match; paper also reports human-inspected lossless and lossy error relaxations.
evaluator.deterministic: Exact-string metric is deterministic; relaxed human error adjudication is not fully automated.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A 100-item-per-condition local-model pilot is plausible within five hours; the bundled model and Transformers path can be used for historical baselines.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: The repository contains a model artifact and dataset; no paid API is required.

candidates.quality_notes: Output-format sensitivity is substantial. Report exact and relaxed scores separately; do not use exact match alone as a claim about reasoning.
candidates.modern_unsaturation: Unknown. Old results are fine-tuned Transformer results, not a modern LLM evaluation.

candidates.name: CLUTRR

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: No official LLM leaderboard found. The original benchmark paper is 2019; a 2022 follow-up reports model accuracy.

published_top_scores.result: 88.8% accuracy on CLUTRR versus 62.9% for its baseline

license.code_and_data: CC-BY-NC 4.0 is stated in the README; GitHub's license detector reports NOASSERTION.

candidates.data_access: Public generator and pre-generated data links; test tasks can hold out relation combinations and noisy facts.

evaluator.deterministic: Yes for fixed data and normalization.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: Generate or select 200 to 500 held-out examples and score them locally within five hours.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: Use a local model and normalize the answer to the relation label.

candidates.quality_notes: Useful systematic-generalization task, but generated kinship patterns may be template-learnable. License is non-commercial.
candidates.modern_unsaturation: Unknown; recent papers still use CLUTRR, but no current official model score was found.

candidates.name: EntailmentBank

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: No leaderboard in the repository; published baseline results are from the 2021 paper.

published_top_scores.metric: Exact whole-proof correctness; paper also reports leaf/step/intermediate F1 and BLEURT

license.data: Public data is linked from AllenAI; a separate data license was not stated in the repository README.

candidates.data_access: Public science questions and proof-tree dataset linked from the repository.

evaluator.metric: Proof-tree overlap, all-correct score, and BLEURT; Task 3 has a separate JSONL scorer.
evaluator.deterministic: Mostly fixed for a pinned BLEURT checkpoint and scorer version; learned BLEURT scoring means it is not a pure symbolic exact-match evaluator.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A small Task 1 pilot may fit, but a fresh Python 3.7 environment plus BLEURT checkpoint download is borderline for five hours.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: Scoring needs no model API. Generate predictions with a local model.

candidates.quality_notes: Best fit if proof quality matters. Legacy Python and learned BLEURT scorer add setup.

candidates.name: SpaRTQA

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: No maintained official leaderboard found; papers include 2021 baselines and later task-specific studies.

published_top_scores.metric: Task-specific Yes/No accuracy and relation-finding precision/recall/F1
published_top_scores.note: A clean, directly comparable top LLM score for the original SpaRTQA splits was not established. Do not substitute ReSQ results.

license.data: The repo links a Google Drive data download; data license was not stated in the README.

candidates.data_access: Dataset download is public via a Drive link; baseline code requires an older Torch/Transformers stack.

evaluator.metric: Exact answer accuracy for Yes/No and choose-object questions; precision/recall/F1 for relation-finding.
evaluator.deterministic: Yes for the fixed labels and metric scripts.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A 100 to 200 item local-model slice is plausible within five hours if the Drive download works; old Transformers 4.0.1 may need a separate environment.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: Use local inference; repository baseline scripts do not require paid LLM calls.

candidates.quality_notes: Different variants and subtask metrics are easy to conflate. Check the exact split before comparing.

candidates.name: FOLIO

repository_activity.last_leaderboard_or_results_update: No official leaderboard found. Paper scores are from 2022; README still says the test leaderboard/test set will be released.

candidates.data_access: GitHub contains labeled train and validation files. The README describes the paper test split as unreleased; check the linked newer dataset before treating the task as held-out.

evaluator.metric: Exact True/False/Unknown accuracy; NL-to-FOL translation has separate structural metrics.
evaluator.deterministic: Yes for label accuracy; translation metric depends on formula normalization.

setup_and_five_hour_fit.estimate: A 100 to 200 labeled development-set slice can be scored within five hours; there is no official current held-out leaderboard path established from GitHub.
setup_and_five_hour_fit.local_no_api_path: Use local inference and a three-label parser.

candidates.quality_notes: High-quality expert logic with verified annotations, but hidden-test availability and contamination make it a weak primary pick.

decision_rules: Treat historical numbers as dated references only, not as proof that current models remain weak.
Prefer fixed, versioned splits and exact or executable scoring; report any LLM-judged metric separately.
Use local model inference only. No paid API, probes, grading calls, or tests were run for this research.
